name: Do I need a designer before a builder for a home addition in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Should I hire an architect or designer before I hire a home builder for an addition in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Should I hire an architect or designer before I hire a home builder for an addition in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an addition in Los Angeles, the safest path is usually to define the design before construction pricing is finalized. The city requires clear plans, and high-end projects often need architectural drawings, structural engineering, and coordination with zoning or plan check requirements. If you hire a builder too early without a solid design, pricing can be vague and change repeatedly as the layout evolves. If you hire design separately, the benefit is a more refined plan and better permit readiness, but the downside is possible disconnect between design intent and construction budget. A design-build team can reduce that gap by designing with cost, feasibility, and permitting in mind from the start. Homeowners should ask whether the builder can coordinate engineering, permit submittals, and revisions, and whether pricing will be based on finalized plans or preliminary concepts.
acceptedAnswer.description: For a home addition in Los Angeles, design usually comes first because the project needs plans, code review, and permit-ready documents before construction can begin. A design-build firm can handle both steps in sequence, which often reduces coordination gaps and redesign delays.
